title: The Situationship Reading

intake.question: How long has this been going on?

options.label: On and off for over a year

intake.question: What do you want from it?

plan.title: Why you're still in it (it's not them)
Where this really is (not where you hope)
What you actually want (not what you text)
How you read mixed signals at 2am
Too much of one thing, none of another
Your line, and when you've crossed it
However it ends, you're fine. Here's why

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. So here's your twist: you don't stay because you're scared. You stay because you think you're in charge of it.

Bom: You can leave any time. That's exactly why you haven't.

Yeon: "I'm in control" is a very comfy chair to sit in while nothing changes.

Pick a date one month from now. On that day, ask yourself three things: am I getting what I want, have I said what I want, did anything change after I said it. Three no's and the chair goes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can walk any time, so you never do. Cute. Choose on purpose.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You give a lot, and you notice everything they don't give back.

Yeon: And then you explain it away. "They're busy." "They're bad at texting." They managed to post a story, babe.

Bom: Staying isn't the problem. Staying quiet is.

One small test this week: say one true thing you want, out loud, in one sentence. Not a hint. Not a meme. Then watch what they do with it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Soft isn't weak. Soft just needs to stop apologising.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You know exactly what you want. You're just refusing to say it first, like it's a card game.

Bom: Saying it first doesn't cost you anything here. There's no prize for holding out. You only find out sooner.

Yeon: And a warning before you write it down. Your list will read like a performance review. "They need to text more." "They need to plan."

Bom: Flip each line so it's about the two of you. Not "they need to text more". Try "I want to hear from you most days." Two people can say yes to that.

Then treat it like any other decision you'd make at work. Write the want. Pick the day you'll say it. Keep the appointment.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Going first isn't losing. It's just getting the answer before everyone else.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart. The want is in there. It's just buried under what you think you're allowed to ask for.

Yeon: You pre-shrink it. You ask for a coffee when you want a weekend. Then you're proud of yourself for being "low pressure".

Bom: Try this. Write the big version, the one you'd ask for if you knew they'd say yes. Then write the small one you were planning to send.

Yeon: The space between those two lines? That's what you've been settling for. Measured. In ink.

Bom: Now say one line from the big version out loud, in your normal voice. It sounds so much more reasonable out loud than it did at 1am. Being someone's person, meeting their friends, a plan for Saturday. That's not too much. That's what a relationship is made of.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the version you'd send if you knew the answer was yes. Then stare at it.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart, so you read signals with total confidence. One late reply and you've written the verdict, the appeal and the sentencing.

Bom: And you send signals you don't notice. Like going quiet on purpose to see what they do.

Yeon: That's not a message. That's a pop quiz they didn't study for.

Bom: For two weeks, swap signals for reports. Busy? Say busy. Liked the date? Say so. Something bugged you? One sentence, then drop it.

When you do catch a signal, check it once before you act on it. "You went quiet this week, all good?" Eight words, and a theory becomes a fact. Your read is good. It's better with one piece of input from the person you're reading.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Going cold to see if they chase isn't a signal. It's a test with no answer key.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart, so every gap in the chat feels like a verdict. Slow reply, you did something wrong. Warm night, everything's fine forever.

Yeon: You're riding a rollercoaster you built yourself and you're not even enjoying the ride.

Bom: Swap reacting for recording. For two weeks, keep a plain note: who texted, who planned, who cancelled. No commentary.

Yeon: No "but they seemed off". Facts only. You're a clerk now.

When the spiral comes anyway, give it a timer. Ten minutes to worry properly, write the worst-case version down, close the note, go wash a mug. Worry with a container shrinks. Worry with a whole evening turns into a theory you half believe by breakfast.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Stop decoding. Keep a boring list for two weeks. The list doesn't lie to you.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart, big risk: you'll run the talk like a contract negotiation. Opening terms. Deadline. A recap of every vague moment since August.

Bom: You'd mean it as honesty. It would land as an ultimatum.

Yeon: Start with what you feel. Then a real question. Then the hardest thing you'll do all year: shut up and wait.

Bom: If their answer isn't the one you wanted, don't argue them into a better one. A yes you had to win doesn't stay won.

Pick the setting like you'd pick a fight you wanted to win, then do the opposite of winning. Side by side beats face to face: a walk, a drive, chopping onions together. Phones away. If they need a few days, agree on the day you'll pick it back up, and actually pick it back up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: If you had to debate them into a yes, it's not a yes. It's a closing argument.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart, big risk: you'll cushion it until it says nothing at all.

Yeon: "I know you're super busy and it's totally fine if not, no pressure, honestly forget I asked." Congratulations, you just answered for them.

Bom: One sentence. The want, no pillows. Then stop talking.

Yeon: If they go vague, you're allowed a follow-up. "Okay, but what does that mean for us?" That's not difficult. That's a question.

Rehearse it once, out loud, alone or with a friend. Not a script, just the main sentence at full size. If your voice wobbles, fine. Wobbly and clear still counts as clear. And book something kind for afterwards, whatever they say. A friend, a film, an early night.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One sentence. No pillows. Then let the silence be their problem for a second.

strong.text:
Bom: Strong chart, so drawing a line is easy for you. Leaving kindly is the hard part.

Yeon: You switch off like a light. One day you're there, the next you're a "seen" receipt and a mystery.

Bom: Add one rule: when you go, you say so. A short message. Not a vanishing act, not a TED talk.

Yeon: Also check your line isn't secretly a trap. You set a boundary, then wait for them to trip it so the decision makes itself.

That's leaving with extra steps. If you already know you're done, they don't have to fail a test first. You're allowed to just decide.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Going? Say so. Two kind sentences beat a disappearing act every time.

weak.text:
Yeon: Soft chart. Your line moves. They step over it, you redraw it two metres back and call it "being understanding".

Bom: So give your line a plan. Not a threat. A plan.

Yeon: "If they cancel last minute three times, I stop making the plans." See? It has numbers. Numbers don't get emotional at midnight.

Bom: Tell one friend your line, too. Not so they police you. So it lives somewhere outside your head.

A friend who can say "you told me three cancellations, this is four" is the gentlest backup there is. It saves you from arguing with yourself at 1am and losing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A boundary with no plan attached is just a wish. Write down what you'll do.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You'll be busy, social and "honestly fine" within a week. Annoyingly resilient.

Bom: The risk isn't falling apart. It's skipping the lesson and running the same episode next spring.

Yeon: So before you move on, one note. What you'll do differently from day one. Ask earlier. Say it sooner. Notice the drift before it's a lifestyle.

Bom: And if this becomes real, keep the talking habit. Strong charts relax once they get the label and stop saying what they need.

A five-minute "how are we doing" every few weeks keeps you out of a brand-new vagueness with a nicer name.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fine in a week? Sure. Write the one lesson down first or this becomes a rerun.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart, so the ending might hit harder than the "situation" seemed to deserve on paper. So much hope went into it. That's not silly.

Yeon: Give yourself a few soft weeks. Friends. Sleep. Things that ask nothing of you. Not his playlist. Not her playlist. Any playlist but that one.

Bom: Keep the lesson tiny and kind: next time, I ask what this is sooner. That's it. You don't need a personality transplant.

Yeon: And if it turns into something real, keep the life you built while it was blurry. Your friends, your plans, your Thursdays.

Being chosen doesn't mean disappearing into someone. Two full lives make a better relationship than one life and a waiting room.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Next time, ask sooner. That's the whole lesson. Be gentle with the rest.

peer_strong.text:
Yeon: Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls that the peer family. Friends, rivals, mirrors.

Bom: It makes you independent, and a little competitive, even in love.

Yeon: In a vague thing, that turns into a standoff. Nobody volunteers to care more. And you are an Olympic athlete at not caring more. On the outside.

Bom: The upside: you'll be okay whatever happens. The downside: two people guarding their independence can drift for a year. Someone goes first. It might as well be the one who can handle either answer.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. So who cares more? Neither of you. Out loud. For a year.

output_strong.text:
Bom: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the output family. Charm, jokes, the perfectly timed flirty text.

Yeon: With a strong chart behind it, you're fun to be undefined with. And you know it.

Bom: Output loves freedom and hates rules, so a label can feel like a cage you'd rather joke about than discuss.

Yeon: Watch the pattern. Great banter, a hundred inside jokes, and not one sentence that says what you want.

Your words are the best thing you've got. Spend one of them on the real thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Elite banter. No clarity. Spend one clever sentence on what you actually want.

wealth_strong.text:
Yeon: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. The wealth family. What you chase, manage, and close.

Bom: A strong chart handles it well. So you're the one who plans, books, decides where you're eating.

Yeon: Which, in a vague thing, means you run the whole operation while they enjoy the ride.

Bom: It can also mean treating this like something to win. So ask yourself honestly. Do you want this person, or do you want to close the deal?

From the inside those feel identical. They lead to very different conversations.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A person isn't a deal to close. Check which one you're chasing.

power_strong.text:
Bom: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that keeps your {dm_el} in check. The power family. Standards, rules, doing things properly.

Yeon: So this situationship bothers you way more than you let on. It's just not how things are done.

Bom: You might even be holding back because naming it feels like admitting you've been in something "improper".

Yeon: It's not improper. It's unfinished. Like a draft with no subject line.

Your standards are useful here. Say them out loud and let them make the call.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your standards are already written down somewhere in you. Read them out. They'll decide.

resource_strong.text:
Yeon: Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. The resource family. Comfort, thinking, safety.

Bom: You're well cushioned, which makes it very easy to think about this forever without moving it an inch.

Yeon: You've analysed their attachment style, your attachment style and their dog's attachment style.

Bom: All that thinking feels productive. Mostly it isn't. Pick one action this week. Any action. A specific plan, or the actual question.

Thinking is your comfort zone. One small move will tell you more than another month of theory.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You've studied this from every angle. Now do one tiny thing instead.

output_weak.text:
Bom: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. The output family. Giving, expressing, performing. On a soft chart, it drains you.

Yeon: So you're the entertainment. Funny texts, thoughtful gifts, staying interesting at all times. For less back.

Bom: It can feel like auditioning for a part nobody's cast yet.

Yeon: Here's a test. How tired are you after you see them?

Good connections leave you a bit fuller. If this one leaves you emptier, that's real information. And it has nothing to do with how hard you try.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You audition every week for a role they never got round to casting.

wealth_weak.text:
Yeon: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. The wealth family. Wanting, reaching, holding on.

Bom: Old saju readers have a phrase for this: a lot to hold, not much behind you holding.

Yeon: So you keep the plans alive, keep the mood nice, keep the whole thing breathing. That's a lot of holding for someone nobody's holding.

Bom: Drop one job this week. Don't plan the next date. See who reaches.

Not a game. Just a way to find out whether the weight is shared.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Skip planning the next one. Watch who reaches. That's information, not a game.

power_weak.text:
Bom: Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}. The power family. Pressure, expectations, being judged.

Yeon: So around them you're on your best behaviour. Not too needy. Not too available. Not too anything. A beige version of you.

Bom: That constant self-editing is pressure, and it's coming from you, not them.

The relief is the element that feeds you: rest, support, people who already like you as you are. Spend more time there. You'll turn up to this person with fewer edits.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You edit yourself around them nonstop. Go hang out where nobody needs a draft.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Bom: In a situationship that shows up as confidence that comes and goes. Some days you're sure of yourself and ready to ask.

Yeon: Other days one slow reply and you're the size of a crumb.

Bom: Both are you. The plenty in your chart is real. It's just not planted where it counts.

So have the big conversation on a good day. After sleep. After food. Ideally after an hour with someone who reminds you who you are.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Some days sure, some days tiny. Book the talk for a sure day.

output_strong.text:
Yeon: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element. The voice.

Bom: A strong chart with no voice feels a lot and says very little.

Yeon: So they might have no idea how much you care. Or how annoyed you are. Your feelings come out as actions. Or silence.

Borrow a voice. Send one "I feel" message on a normal Wednesday. Not mid-crisis. Just a Wednesday. You'll need that voice soon, because the next chapter is the talk.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}, no voice. They honestly don't know what you feel. Tell them.

wealth_strong.text:
Bom: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element. Going after a specific result.

Yeon: Lots of drive, no destination. Which is exactly how a situationship drifts on your watch.

Bom: You're not pushing it anywhere. So if you want it to go somewhere, pick the place on purpose.

What would you like this to be in three months? Decide. Then act like someone headed there. The first stop on that road is a conversation. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pick a destination. Drifting nicely is still drifting.

power_strong.text:
Yeon: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element. The rulebook.

Bom: Strong chart, no rulebook. You make it up as you go. Brilliant for fun, terrible for clarity.

Yeon: A situationship is literally what happens when nobody sets terms. So set some.

Small ones. "We see each other once a week." "We tell each other if someone else is in the picture." Structure isn't unromantic. It's what lets the romance stick around. And the first rule gets set in one conversation. You know the one. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No rulebook in your chart. That's how you ended up here. Write two rules.

resource_strong.text:
Bom: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element. Comfort. Reassurance.

Yeon: You're strong with no cushion, so you cope alone and look great doing it.

Bom: Which means you never show you need reassurance. So you never get any.

Ask for one small thing. A text when they land. A plan made more than a day ahead. How they handle a small need shows you how they'd handle a big one. The big one is coming up: the talk.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for one small comfort. How they treat it tells you plenty.

output_weak.text:
Bom: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element. Saying things out loud.

Yeon: On a soft chart that's handy. You don't burn yourself out talking.

Bom: But you rarely say what you want. So this can stay unnamed simply because you never named it.

Practise on paper. Draft the message in your notes tonight, read it in the morning, then decide. The next chapter helps you write it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write it in your notes tonight. Reread it with coffee. Then decide.

wealth_weak.text:
Yeon: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element. Going after things.

Bom: On a soft chart that can feel restful. You don't chase. You don't grab.

Yeon: The catch: you wait for the relationship to steer itself, because you don't feel allowed to touch the wheel.

You're allowed. Start small. Suggest the plan. Pick the place. Name the next date. Then the big steer, which is where we're going next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're allowed to steer. Start by choosing the restaurant. Seriously.

power_weak.text:
Bom: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element. Outside pressure.

Yeon: On a soft chart, that's one less weight. Nice. Also, nobody taught you that asking for terms is normal.

Bom: It is. Wanting to know what you are to someone is a standard, not a demand.

Borrow a gentle rule. Pick a date, and ask what this is by then. What you'll actually say on that date? Turn the page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wanting to know where you stand isn't demanding. It's a basic standard.

resource_weak.text:
Bom: No {miss_el} in your visible pillars. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element. Your built-in supply of reassurance.

Yeon: Which is why mixed signals hit you like a bus. No cushion, so every wobble lands straight on you.

Bom: So build the cushion somewhere else. Friends who reply. Routines that steady you. A life that would still feel full if this ended.

With that in place, their texts stop running your mood. And you'll walk into the talk standing up. That's next.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Build your cushion elsewhere: friends, routine, sleep. Their texts shrink.

none_strong.text:
Bom: All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars, even if a few are hiding in the branches. On a strong chart, that means range.

Yeon: Flirt, plan, push, wait, walk. You've done all five. This month.

Bom: The trouble is cycling through every mode without committing to one.

This week, pick one on purpose. If clarity is what you want, choose direct, and stay direct until you get an answer. What direct sounds like coming from you is the next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Flirty Monday, distant Wednesday, sulky Friday. Pick one mode and live there.

none_weak.text:
Bom: All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars, even if a few are hiding in the branches. On a soft chart, that's more range than confidence.

Yeon: You can be playful, warm, firm or patient. And you always pick whichever feels least risky.

Bom: Try picking what fits instead. If the moment needs firm, be firm. Gently.

You own the tool. You've just left it in the drawer. And that drawer is exactly what the talk is about. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: There's a firm version of you in there. Let it out. Gently.

resource.title: What keeps you steady: {helper_el}
resource.text:
Bom: Every chart has one element that brings it back to centre. For your soft {dm_el} chart, it's the one that feeds you: {helper_el}.

Yeon: Translation: feeling okay before their next text, instead of because of it.

Bom: When you're topped up on {helper_el}, you ask clearer questions and take vague answers less personally.

Charge your own battery before the conversation, so you're not running on their mood.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your steadying element is {helper_el}. Fill up on it before you open the chat.

peer.title: What keeps you steady: more {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Bom: Every chart has one element that brings it back to centre. Yours already has plenty of support on paper, so what helps most is your own element, {helper_el}.

Yeon: That means peers. Friends who are on your side and will tell you honestly if this sounds good or sounds like a podcast episode.

Bom: A soft chart with lots of support can overthink alone. Company pulls you out of your head and back into your life.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your element is {helper_el}. Call the friend who'll tell you the truth, not a guru.

output.title: What gets you unstuck: {helper_el}
output.text:
Bom: Every chart has one element that brings it back to centre. A strong {dm_el} chart needs somewhere for all that force to go. For you, it's {helper_el}, the element your Day Master produces.

Yeon: In plain English: say the thing. Make the plan. Send the message.

Bom: You get stuck when you hold your strength in and wait. You get unstuck the second you move, even if the move is one honest sentence.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. You get unstuck by saying it.

wealth.title: What makes it real for you: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Bom: Every chart has one element that brings it back to centre. Yours is strong and already talks plenty, so what helps is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master works on.

Yeon: Meaning: make it concrete. A specific plan. A specific date. A question with a yes or no answer.

Bom: You do best when the blurry stuff becomes something you can hold. So turn it into something you can hold.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. Make it real: a date, a question, an answer.

wood.text: In real life, {helper_el} is growth that belongs to you. A class, a project, a plan that points forward, long walks somewhere green. When your own life is growing, a vague relationship stops being the most interesting thing in it. Keep that in your pocket. The next pages get personal.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood is growth that's yours. Start one thing this week that has a future.

fire.text: In real life, {helper_el} is warmth and being seen. Nights out with friends, saying what you think, sunlight, laughing too loud, letting people see you excited. You read situations more clearly when you're not hiding. Remember that. It matters a lot in what comes next.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire is warmth. Go where people light up when you walk in.

earth.text: In real life, {helper_el} is steadiness. Regular meals, a home you like being in, a routine that doesn't bend for anyone's last-minute text, friends who show up. A steady base makes unsteady people much easier to see clearly. Hold that thought. You'll want it in a minute.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth is routine. Keep your plans even when they text at 9pm asking "u up".

metal.text: In real life, {helper_el} is clarity and edges. Lists, decisions, a tidy desk, saying no without a three-paragraph essay, finishing things. When your days have edges, you notice much faster when someone keeps blurring them. Keep that sharpness. Two more pages and you'll need it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal is edges. Tidy desk, tidy calendar, one tidy question.

water.text: In real life, {helper_el} is rest and reflection. Sleep, slow evenings, a journal, a long walk with no podcast. You work out what you want in the stillness, not halfway through a chat. Bring that stillness with you. The next part asks for it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water is stillness. Your answer turns up on the quiet walk, not in the chat.

rat.text: The Rat sits closest to your heart: clever, private, awake at night. You figured this person out fast and you're keeping your cards close. Maybe too close. They can't answer a question you never ask.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat heart: you've got a whole strategy and no actual sentence.

ox.text: The Ox guards your heart: slow, steady, loyal past the point of sense. You don't attach fast, but once you do you hold the line for months. Ask whether the line is worth it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox heart: slow to trust, impossible to shake off. Choose wisely.

tiger.text: The Tiger sits in your heart: brave, independent, bored by games. Part of you wants to just ask them straight. Another part refuses to look like the one who wanted it first. Tigers hate losing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger heart: you'd jump off a cliff before you'd say "I like you" first.

rabbit.text: The Rabbit lives close to your heart: gentle, charming, allergic to conflict. You'll keep the peace even if the peace is starving you. Wanting clarity isn't starting a fight.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit heart: asking isn't attacking. Promise.

dragon.text: The Dragon guards your heart: big dreams, big standards. You want something grand and you're quietly insulted this is the version on offer. Trust that instinct.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon heart in a half-relationship. You're cosplaying low standards.

snake.text: The Snake sits closest to your heart: intuitive, private, strategic. You've already read this person completely. You're just waiting to see if they'll prove you wrong.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snake heart: you clocked them on day one. Stop pretending you didn't.

horse.text: The Horse lives in your heart: passionate, restless, needs to run. The intensity of this thing is half the appeal. The other half is that nobody's fenced you in. Yet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse heart: you want fire and freedom. Ask for both, out loud.

goat.text: The Goat guards your heart: gentle, homey, hungry for reassurance. You need to feel safe to open up, and a situationship is built to never feel quite safe. That's not you being needy. That's the setup.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat heart: wanting reassurance is normal. Ask for it.

monkey.text: The Monkey sits in your heart: clever, playful, a little restless. The banter is the best part, and you're scared that defining it will kill the fun. It won't. Fun survives labels.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey heart: you'd rather keep the bit going than say one sincere thing.

rooster.text: The Rooster guards your heart: proud, precise, sees every flaw. You've noticed every red flag, catalogued it, and stayed anyway. Your standards are fine. It's your follow-through.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rooster heart: you've got a full list of their flaws and still no exit.

dog.text: The Dog lives close to your heart: loyal, protective, principled. You decided early that they're worth it, and you're loyal to that decision even when the evidence wobbles. Loyalty wants a clear person to be loyal to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog heart: loyal before they've earned it. Ask what you're guarding.

pig.text: The Pig sits in your heart: sweet, generous, trusting. You give people the benefit of the doubt over and over. Give yourself some too. You're allowed to want more than this.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig heart: your trust is a gift. Don't hand it out on a loop.

day_branch_heading: Who you let in close: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

weeks.text:
Bom: Weeks, not months. Honestly? That's not a situationship yet. That's a beginning, and beginnings are allowed to be blurry.

Yeon: Put down the label maker. There's nothing to label yet.

Bom: The better question right now isn't "what are we". It's "who am I around them". More relaxed or more edited? More yourself or more careful?

If the answers feel good, enjoy it and keep your own calendar busy. You can name it once there's something to name.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A few weeks is a start, not a crisis. Keep your Saturdays full anyway.

months.text:
Bom: Months in is exactly when people start wanting to know what this is. You're not needy. You're on schedule.

Yeon: And by now you have evidence. Lots of it. You've just been reading your feelings instead of the evidence.

Bom: How do they act when plans change? Do they say "next summer" or only "this weekend"? Have you met a single person in their life?

Feelings tell you what you want. Evidence tells you what's happening. Read the evidence first.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Months in, wanting a name for it is normal. Check the evidence before the feelings.

half.text:
Yeon: Half a year of "we'll see". At this point the blurriness isn't an accident. Someone's choosing it. Maybe both of you.

Bom: Which isn't automatically bad. But it means the vagueness is doing a job for someone.

Yeon: Is it protecting them from commitment? Or protecting you from hearing no?

Six months buys you the right to a straight answer. And it's long enough that not asking has quietly become a choice too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Six months of maybe is a decision somebody keeps making. Find out who.

onoff.text:
Bom: A year of on and off. That's a loop, and loops have a rhythm. Close, drift, silence, then a reunion that feels like proof.

Yeon: Every comeback feels like a sign. It's not a sign. It's the chorus.

Bom: Nobody doubts you have feelings. The real question is whether anything changes during the gaps.

If every round looks like the last one, the pattern is the relationship. It keeps running until somebody steps off.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: On and off for a year isn't fate. It's a loop. Loops run till someone steps off.

unsaid.text:
Bom: However long it's been, try this. Count the times you've asked yourself what this is.

Yeon: Once or twice? It's young. Let it grow.

Bom: Lost count? Then your head already answered. You want to know.

And every week you wait after that point costs you a little more than it costs them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lost count of how often you've wondered? Then you already want the answer.

me_strong.text:
Bom: You start most of the chats. With your strong chart that's just you. See it, want it, go.

Yeon: Nothing wrong with that. But are they matching you, or politely keeping up like a group project partner?

Bom: Try one week of not starting. Not a punishment. A measurement.

If they fill the space, lovely. If it stays empty, you've learned something big without one argument. And that's not even the main thing you need to know. That comes when we get to what you actually want.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Don't text first for one week. Not revenge. Just data.

me_weak.text:
Bom: You start most of the chats. With a soft chart, it can feel like the connection only exists while you're holding it up.

Yeon: Like a tent. In wind. And you're the pole.

Bom: That's exhausting, and it hides how invested they really are. So step back a little. Reply warmly when they write. Just don't open every conversation.

It'll feel risky. It's also the only way to find out if they'd reach for you. Which brings us to the scarier question: what do you even want from them? Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Answer warmly. Just let them start a few. You'll learn so much.

them_strong.text:
Yeon: They text first. You reply when it suits you. And you call that "being chill".

Bom: Being chased feels nice. But it can leave them guessing whether you care at all.

Yeon: That's how half of all situationships stall. One person chasing, one person enjoying the cardio.

Bom: If you like them, show it once, unprompted. A random text from you would land hard, exactly because you never send one.

So what would you even send? That depends on what you actually want. Next chapter, we find out.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Text them first once, out of nowhere. Rare warmth from you hits different.

them_weak.text:
Bom: They usually reach out first. That's reassuring and confusing at once. They want you, so why is it still unnamed?

Yeon: Getting texted isn't the same as getting chosen. But it's not nothing either.

Bom: Their effort means you're in a stronger position than you feel. You can ask a direct question without "pushing your luck".

Yeon: You have luck. Use it.

Before you ask them anything, though, you need your own answer first. That's the next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They keep coming back to the chat. You're holding better cards than you think.

even.text:
Bom: About even. That's healthy, actually. You're both invested enough to start conversations.

Yeon: So this isn't about interest. It's about two adults too shy to say a noun.

Bom: Which makes the talk lower risk than it feels. You're not asking them to care. They already show it. You're asking what to call it.

And what you'd want to call it is a whole other question. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Even effort means real interest. All that's missing is a word for it.

unsaid.text:
Bom: Whoever starts the chat, watch how it ends.

Yeon: Who always says goodnight first? Who makes the next plan? Who goes quiet mid-thread and reappears Tuesday?

Bom: Endings tell you more than openings. If one person always closes the door, that's information, even when every hello feels warm.

Watch it for a week. Then we'll talk about what you actually want from this. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Notice who always ends the chat. Goodbyes say more than hellos.

official_strong.text:
Yeon: You said "something official". Great. You've told a comic. Now tell the human.

Bom: Your chart can take a no better than you think. And a clear yes is worth the risk.

Yeon: Just don't make "official" mean your version only. Ask what it looks like for them.

Two people defining it together lasts longer than one person announcing it. Before you say anything, though, look at how you've been reading their signals. That's the next chapter, and it's a bit embarrassing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Telling a reading is easy. Now tell the person with the actual phone.

official_weak.text:
Bom: You said you want something official. That's completely fair. You don't owe anyone a justification.

Yeon: The soft-chart habit is asking so quietly it sounds optional. "No pressure if not!" It's not optional for you. Stop phrasing it like a survey.

Bom: You can say it kindly and still mean it. "I'm hoping for a proper relationship with you." Then listen.

But first, a confession about how you read their texts. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wanting it official is reasonable. Ask kindly and mean every word.

casual_strong.text:
Bom: You said you want to keep it casual. That's allowed. It might be exactly right for you right now.

Yeon: You're allowed to overrule your own chart. It's a comic, not a parole officer.

Bom: One check, though. Do they know it's casual for you? Most situationship pain comes from one person thinking it's heading somewhere.

Yeon: Clear casual is kind. Vague casual is how someone ends up crying in a car park.

And if you're so clear, why do their mixed signals still get to you? Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Casual is fine. Casual and vague is how somebody gets hurt. Say it plainly.

casual_weak.text:
Bom: You said casual. Fine. Just check casual is a want and not a shield.

Yeon: "I'm totally fine with casual" can be a very elegant way to never hear a no to something bigger.

Bom: If casual really suits you, have fun with it and keep your own life busy. If a part of you is hoping for more, let that part speak. Even if it's only to you, in the shower.

And notice how hard their mixed signals hit you. That tells us a lot. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Is casual what you want, or just the safest thing to ask for?

out_strong.text:
Yeon: You said you want out. Strong chart, so you can do this cleanly. In words. Not by fading like a phone at 3%.

Bom: "I've enjoyed this, and I'm going to step back." You don't owe a long explanation. You owe a clear one.

Yeon: Then follow through. Don't reopen it on a lonely Tuesday to check if they're sad.

Before you send anything, look at the signals that kept you here this long. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Want out? Use words. Short, kind, final. And no "just checking in" next month.

out_weak.text:
Bom: You said you want out. That's brave to admit. And it's allowed even if they did nothing terrible.

Yeon: "They're not a villain" is not a reason to stay. Wanting more for yourself is a good enough reason to go.

Bom: If face to face feels too big, a kind message is fine. And expect a wobble afterwards. Missing someone you chose to leave doesn't mean you chose wrong.

There's a reason the signals kept pulling you back in, though. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You can leave someone who did nothing wrong. Wanting more counts.

unsure_strong.text:
Yeon: You don't know what you want? You. The person with opinions about everyone's fonts.

Bom: That's unusual for a strong chart, which makes it worth listening to. Maybe you like them but not the setup. Maybe the setup but not them.

Yeon: Quick test. Picture them, fully committed. Then picture this exact arrangement with someone else.

Whichever picture pulls you is your answer. And how you've been reading their signals might explain the confusion. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Them, fully committed. Or this setup, with someone new. Which picture wins?

unsure_weak.text:
Bom: You don't know what you want yet. That's okay. With a soft chart it often means you've tuned into what they want for so long, your own channel went quiet.

Yeon: You know their usual order at three different cafés. You don't know your own opinion. Classic.

Bom: Give your want a microphone. A few days of not checking the chat for them. Notice which parts of them you actually miss, and which parts you just miss checking.

Your want is still in there. And the way you read their signals has been drowning it out. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Phone face down for a few days. Your own answer gets louder.

weeks.speaker: yeon
weeks.text: A few weeks, you said. A few weeks and you're already reading a comic about it. Noted.

months.speaker: bom
months.text: A few months. Long enough to have a song. Short enough that you still can't say "we".

half.speaker: yeon
half.text: Six months or more. That's not a situationship anymore. That's a lease with no contract.

onoff.speaker: yeon
onoff.text: On, off, on again, for more than a year. You two don't have a status. You have seasons.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You skipped "how long". Which tells me it's been longer than you'd like to admit.

me.speaker: yeon
me.text: You said you reach out first. Mostly. So you're carrying the whole chat and calling it "just being friendly".

them.speaker: bom
them.text: You said they reach out first. So they keep coming back. That means something. We'll find out what.

even.speaker: yeon
even.text: About even, you said. Fifty-fifty texting and zero-zero clarity. Impressive balance.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You didn't say who texts first. That's okay. I'll read it from you instead.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

mu-earth.why-you-stay:
You stay because it's stable. Not great, not terrible. Predictable. And predictable feels safe to a mountain.

Bom: You don't need fireworks. You need consistency.

Yeon: So you settled for consistently unclear.

Bom: You also hate starting over. New people mean new explaining.

Yeon: "I don't want to start from zero" is how you've stayed at four out of ten for this long.
mu-earth.what-you-want:
You want someone you can actually count on. You'll never say it. You'll just keep being countable-on and hope they catch the hint.

Yeon: You show up. You keep your word. You remember their mum's surgery date. And they reply "sorry, crazy week" for the fourth week running.

Bom: Being reliable yourself doesn't make them reliable back. That's not how it transfers.

Bom: So name it plainly. Plans that hold. Being the only one. Someone who shows up when it matters, not just when it's handy.

If that isn't happening, more patience from you isn't the fix. It's more of the same. Wanting a solid floor doesn't make you demanding. It makes you clear about what you'd build on.
mu-earth.mixed-signals:
Mixed signals? You ignore them and hold your course. Unbothered. Very mountain.

Yeon: Also how you end up sitting in something for eight months that never moved an inch.

Bom: Not reacting keeps you calm. But stop waiting for one clear signal and look at the pattern instead.

Yeon: Has anything grown since month one? Met their friends? Plans further out than Thursday?

Mountains notice erosion slowly. Check the landscape honestly. If nothing's changed, the stillness is the signal, and you can stop waiting for a louder one.
mu-earth.the-talk:
Your talk can be straightforward, almost practical. That suits you.

Bom: Pick a calm moment. A walk, side by side. "I like what we have, and I'd like it to be more defined. Where are you at?"

Yeon: The risk: you say it so flat they think you're asking about the bus timetable.

Bom: So add one honest sentence on top. "This matters to me."

Then listen without deciding in advance what their answer means. And give yourself a day before you decide anything. You process slowly, and that's allowed.
mu-earth.your-line:
Your line is being taken for granted. People lean on mountains without thinking.

Yeon: You're always available. You always move your plans. You have zero say in what this is. Basically furniture with feelings.

Bom: Decide what effort you need back, in concrete terms. Write down two or three examples.

If you can't remember the last time you saw one, that tells you plenty. When it's missing week after week, step away calmly. Mountains don't chase. The right people climb toward them on purpose.
mu-earth.either-way:
Whatever they say, you'll stand.

Bom: If they want more, it'll be built on something solid, because you are solid.

Yeon: If not, you'll take time. Way more than you show anyone. Your friends will think you're fine. You'll be reorganising your sock drawer at midnight.

Bom: So tell one friend how you're actually doing. Real words, not "I'm fine". Even mountains need company.

You've been the steady thing for other people for years. Let someone be steady for you for a week. Then shift one small thing, a new route, a new class, so your life feels like it's moving too.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: You're so steady. Whatever happens, you're the constant. That's rare.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: They always know you'll be there. That's exactly why they don't hurry.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Mountains don't move. That's why your feelings are so real once they're there.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Then say "this matters to me". Out loud. With your actual mouth.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Read the pattern, not the one good night.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Has anything moved since month one? Check the map, Mountain.

spring.intro: A mountain in spring, with trees pushing through it from every side. Life tested you early. That's why you're so steady now, and also why "relax" sounds to you like a trick.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You became the calm one because someone had to.

summer.intro: A summer mountain, warmed all the way through. Solid, generous, the one everyone leans on. You give off safety without trying. People tell you things they've never told anyone, and you never repeat them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: People feel safe with you within five minutes. Rare.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain, showing its stone. You turn your weight into output: work done, things built, problems quietly solved. You don't talk about feelings much. You show them by fixing the shelf.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Love language: unasked-for repairs. Every time.

winter.intro: A mountain in winter, holding back the river. You manage things: money, plans, other people's chaos. Very good at it. The cost is that you rarely let anything thaw, including you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not cold. You're frozen on purpose. Different.

earth.intro: A mountain born in Earth's own weeks. Triple solid. You don't move unless you want to, and you almost never want to. Your loyalty is legendary. So is the time it takes you to change your mind.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Persuading you is a geological process.

mu-earth.strong:
Bom: Your mountain sits on solid ground, Mu. Steady, secure, slow to change course.

Yeon: So either you're too comfy to push, or you've decided what this is in your head and you're acting like it's settled. Without telling them.

Bom: The strong-Earth blind spot: you're sure, so you assume they are too.

Yeon: Ask out loud. A mountain that never speaks can't be surprised. It also can't be met halfway.

Steady and talkative can live in the same person. Promise.
mu-earth.weak:
Bom: Thin support in your chart, Mu. You hold steady by sheer effort.

Yeon: And you're soaking up all their uncertainty and calling it patience. A sponge with excellent posture.

Bom: The blind spot is believing that if you stay solid long enough, they'll settle on you.

Yeon: People can walk on solid ground forever without ever buying it.

Your needs count as much as your patience. Tell them what you want, and decide privately how long you're willing to wait.

texting.heading: Your texts are all logistics, zero feelings
texting.text:
You text rarely and reliably, Mu. You reply when you said you would. You never send sixteen messages about nothing.

Yeon: "8pm ok." "Parking is round the back." A love letter, if the love letter was a parking notice.

Bom: Your steadiness is attractive. But to someone more expressive, it can read as distance. They may honestly not know if you like them.

Yeon: And you read their texts so generously. They go quiet for four days and you think, "they're busy". Saint-like. Also, sometimes, a very long wait.

Add one line of warmth to your next practical text. "See you at 8. Looking forward to it." The second sentence costs you nothing and tells them everything. And why feelings come out of you so slowly? That's in your balance. Next page.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Add "looking forward to it" to your logistics text, Mu. Then watch.

script.heading: Practical words, one feeling, Mountain
script.text:
You'll want to ask practically. So let practical help.

Bom: "I like you, and I'm the kind of person who likes to know where things stand. What are we doing here?"

Yeon: Very you. Now the hard bit: when they turn it back on you, you need a feeling sentence ready.

Bom: "I'd like to be your partner, officially." Mountains don't make speeches. You don't need one.

Yeon: And if they hedge, don't just absorb it and keep waiting. Say it steady: "I'm not in a rush, but I'm not going to wait forever."

Calm, solid, and clear about the limit. Pure you. But there's a blind spot that's been making the waiting easy. Next chapter.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, telling them you won't wait around forever is allowed. Calmly.

dealbreaker.heading: The ground you won't build on, Mountain
dealbreaker.text:
Your secret dealbreaker is unreliability. Not wild behaviour. Just the steady drip of late, cancelled, vague.

Yeon: You can carry a lot. You won't build on ground that keeps shifting. The problem is you'll tolerate it for ages, because patience is your factory setting.

Bom: So put a number on it. Three cancelled plans without a real reason, and you stop making plans.

The green flag is the plainest one: they show up when they said they would, again and again. For a mountain, consistency is romance. And after the line? The last chapter is where you get to breathe.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Three cancellations, Mu. Then you stop making plans. That's the rule.

mu-earth.title: You're not waiting for them. You're just not moving. Different.
mu-earth.text:
You don't chase. You don't beg. You just stay exactly where you are and let them come to you. Very dignified. Very slow.

Bom: You're patient because you're secure.

Yeon: You're patient because asking would mean feeling something on purpose.
mu-earth.end: Yeon: And there's one thing about mountains this person figured out very fast. Next page.

cliff.mu-earth: Yeon: Where it stands, Mountain: they know you won't leave, so | they've stopped trying to make you stay. Read that twice.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: No speech required. One sentence, and the nerve not to take it back.

gap-wood-and-mu-earth.title: Shoving a mountain to check if it's interested
gap-wood-and-mu-earth.you_are_a:
You suggest the weekend trip, the new restaurant, dinner with your friends. Mu says "maybe". Then nothing. Then, four hours later, a perfectly sincere reply that moves nothing forward.

Yeon: You read stillness as rejection. Mu reads your pushing as pressure. Great system.

Bom: A situationship can be very comfy for a mountain. Same café, same Sunday, no big talks. You want growth.

Yeon: And own this: you quietly improve the people you date. Better job. Better gym. Better sofa. Mu feels that as roots cracking rock.

For the talk, lower the pressure and raise the clarity. Don't pitch a future. Ask one thing: "I'd like us to be official. Is that something you want, or do you like it as it is?" Give Mu room to answer, and agree that slow isn't the same as no. If you can't live with the answer, that's information too. Which brings us to your line.
gap-wood-and-mu-earth.you_are_b:
Gap wants to grow somewhere, and right now they're growing toward you. Flattering on Monday. Exhausting by Thursday.

Yeon: A trip. A gig. Meeting the friends. A new hobby "we could do together". You like them. You also like your Sunday exactly as it is.

Bom: So you say maybe and reply once you've actually thought about it, hours later. To you, that's respect. To Gap, it's a closed door.

Yeon: And Gap tries to improve what they love. If you feel lightly managed, you're allowed to say so.

Bom: In a situationship, steadiness without words reads as "not interested".

Gap needs your position out loud, not guessed from your silence. "I like you. I move slowly, but I'm not going anywhere. I'd like this to be real." If Gap's pace is too much, say that too, kindly and specifically. Mountains don't have to move. They do have to speak. Next: your line.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu's four-hour reply is sincere. It just runs on mountain time.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, stop renovating the mountain. It was never on the market.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, say it out loud once. Silence isn't a full sentence.

1.speaker: yeon
1.text: Gap keeps renovating the mountain. It was never on the market.

2.speaker: bom
2.text: Mu needs to say it out loud once. Ask Mu to. Silence isn't a full sentence.

eul-wood-and-mu-earth.title: Climbing the mountain the sneaky way
eul-wood-and-mu-earth.you_are_a:
Mu is the mountain you've decided to climb. And you're doing it like a vine: sideways, gently, with a lot of charm.

Yeon: Funny reel. "Thinking of you." A dog in a raincoat. Three hours later: "ha. nice." Mountain or wall? Hard to tell.

Bom: Translation: Mu's "ok" is warm. It just arrives at mountain speed.

Yeon: The drift starts when you work around Mu instead of talking to them. Charm. Then hints. Then inviting their best friend so Mu has to come.

Bom: Mu notices manoeuvres, and Mu goes hard when it feels handled. You may find Mu slow. Mu may find your social calendar a lot.

Skip the clever route and go straight up: "I like you, and I want this to be a real relationship. What do you think?" Then let the silence sit. Mu thinks before answering. A slow answer from a mountain is a considered one. Next page: your line.
eul-wood-and-mu-earth.you_are_b:
Eul climbs into your life slowly, then everywhere at once. Morning stickers. A voice note about their coworker. A picnic with nine strangers.

Yeon: It's a lot. Also lovely, like ivy on a stone wall. You reply when you've got something real to say. Hours later. Two words.

Bom: To you, that's sincere. To Eul, it looks like you're barely in it.

Yeon: So Eul tries to read you. Charm. Hints. Gently arranging things so you end up at the picnic. You notice, you dig in, and a nice thing becomes a negotiation.

Bom: Your steadiness is real. Without words, Eul can't see it.

No speech needed. One clear sentence and maybe a heart emoji, which costs you very little and means a lot: "I'm not much of a texter, but I'm serious about you. I'd like us to be official." Then say it again in person. A mountain's word weighs more face to face. Your line is next.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, your "ok" is warm. Eul just can't hear it from down here.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Eul, inviting their best friend so they have to show up? Cute. Also sneaky.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Straight up the mountain, Eul. No scenic route.

0.speaker: bom
0.text: Mu's "ok" is warm, Eul. You just can't hear it from down there.

1.speaker: yeon
1.text: Eul invites your best friend so you have to come. Cute. Also sneaky.

byeong-fire-and-mu-earth.title: You send twelve texts. They send one, and mean it.
byeong-fire-and-mu-earth.you_are_a:
Mu is the sun's favourite mountain. Solid, calm, quietly impressive. You warm them up. They make you feel steady. You sleep better around Mu, and for a sun, that's not nothing.

Yeon: Then the tempo problem. You send plans, jokes, a photo of the sky, an idea for Saturday, a better idea for Saturday.

Bom: Mu replies once. One sincere sentence. Hours later. You wonder if they're bored. More likely Mu just doesn't do volume.

Yeon: You want to go out and celebrate. Mu wants to stay in and order the same curry. Again.

Bom: After weeks of you suggesting and Mu declining, you feel like you're doing all the running. You get louder. Mu goes still. You get louder still.

Count quality, not quantity. Then ask calmly, on one of Mu's stay-in nights: "I like you, and I'd like us to be official. Would you want that?" Let Mu answer slowly. A mountain's yes doesn't come with fireworks, but it holds. Next: your line.
byeong-fire-and-mu-earth.you_are_b:
Byeong walks into your quiet life like a festival. Night market. A seaside trip booked on a Tuesday. You enjoy more of it than you expected.

Yeon: You also need an entire Sunday to recover.

Bom: Byeong sends twelve messages. You send one, and mean every word. Byeong might read your one as half-hearted.

Yeon: Byeong is buzzing about something and you reply "sounds good". To a sun, that lands like a cloud with a clipboard.

Bom: And in tension, Byeong flares and you go silent, which makes Byeong flare more. Your steadiness can read as "not impressed".

You don't have to match the energy. Just make your interest visible. A quick "haha" or a heart goes further than you'd think. Then say it in person: "I'm not loud about it, but I really like you. I'd like this to be a relationship. Is that where you are?" Byeong loves being told things. Tell them. Then: your line.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, a quick "haha" keeps the sun shining. Cheap. Effective.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, twelve texts per reply is just Mu's exchange rate. Accept it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Count quality, not quantity. That one sentence was sincere. All of it.

0.speaker: bom
0.text: A quick "haha" from Mu would keep you shining. Ask for that much.

1.speaker: yeon
1.text: Byeong sends twelve texts per reply. That's just your exchange rate, Mu.

jeong-fire-and-mu-earth.title: Your paragraph. Their "yes, it was good".
jeong-fire-and-mu-earth.you_are_a:
Mu is the mountain temple your lantern was looking for. Steady. Quiet. Safe. Always replies, even if it's three words four hours later. Fixes your shelf without being asked.

Yeon: Then you send a long, heartfelt message about your evening together. Mu replies "yes, it was good." You read it four times hunting for more.

Bom: There isn't more. And also, for Mu, there was a lot in that sentence.

Yeon: You ask what this is, Mu says "it's fine" and means it completely. Somehow not reassuring.

Bom: Go quiet because you're hurt, and Mu may not notice until it's a fire. Your depth doesn't register unless it's said out loud.

Use the simplest repair there is. One sentence: "I want us to be official." Then ask Mu to say back what they heard. Feeling heard does most of the work. And read Mu's reliability as the love it is. Next: your line.
jeong-fire-and-mu-earth.you_are_b:
Jeong brings warmth into your steady life. A lantern in the temple. They notice, they remember, they send long messages about how a walk with you felt.

Yeon: You reply "it was a great day" and mean every word. Jeong reads it six times looking for what's underneath.

Bom: You don't flood people with emotion. Jeong needs some of it out loud.

Yeon: Jeong asks where this is going. You say "it's fine". Complete reassurance, in your language. In Jeong's, it sounds like you didn't hear the question.

Bom: And if Jeong goes quiet because something hurt, you may not notice until it flares. Jeong may not count your reliability unless you name it.

mu-earth-and-gi-earth.title: The invisible work happening in the valley
mu-earth-and-gi-earth.you_are_a:
Gi is the valley next to your mountain. Soft where you're solid. Attentive where you're steady. They remember your mum's name and sort things you never noticed needed sorting.

Yeon: And Gi does nearly all the invisible work. Check-ins. Plans. Smoothing.

Bom: You reply short and solid, and assume Gi would say if something were wrong. Gi assumes you'd ask if you cared.

Yeon: So Gi worries about what this is, and you say "don't worry about it". For a Gi, the least comforting sentence in English.

Bom: If it ever comes out, it'll sound like "I feel like I'm doing everything". And that might genuinely surprise you. Your calm can read as not noticing.

Ask a question back for once. Several, actually. Then: "I know I'm not very expressive, but I'm serious about you. I want us to be a couple." And thank Gi, specifically, for one thing they did that you never mentioned. Next: your line.
mu-earth-and-gi-earth.you_are_b:
Mu is the mountain beside your valley. Steady, protective, unbothered by almost everything.

Yeon: You're worrying. Mu shrugs: "it'll be fine." Half of you relaxes. Half of you wants to scream into a cushion.

Bom: You ask the caring questions, plan the weekends, remember what Mu forgets. Mu replies briefly and seems happy. Mu may honestly not see how much you're carrying.

Yeon: Because you carry it so quietly. You both dodge conflict, so "what are we" stays unasked while you keep doing all the small things.

Bom: Mu reads silence as "all good". You assume Mu would bring it up if Mu cared.

Say what you need before you're too tired to: "I really like you, and I've been doing a lot of the work here. I'd like us to be official and share it. Can we?" Trust that Mu's brevity isn't indifference. And ask Mu to ask you questions sometimes. Then: your line.

mu-earth-and-gyeong-metal.title: They want an answer tonight. You want a week.
mu-earth-and-gyeong-metal.you_are_a:
Gyeong is the ore inside your mountain. Strength protecting strength. No drama, no games, no 47-message threads.

Yeon: Short texts both sides. It works. Mostly.

Bom: The trouble is pace. Gyeong wants to decide tonight. You want to sleep on it, possibly for a week.

Yeon: Gyeong asks "so what are we doing" and you go still. Gyeong reads still as stalling and gets blunter. It bruises you more than you show, so you dig in. Two proud people, nose to nose, neither moving first.

Bom: Neither of you apologises easily, so small standoffs last. Your patience can look like reluctance.

You don't have to answer instantly. You do have to answer. Tell Gyeong your timing: "Give me until Sunday, I want to think properly." Then on Sunday: "I'd like us to be together. I'm slow, not unsure." And add one personal line to your texts each day. Efficient with warmth beats efficient. Next: your line.
mu-earth-and-gyeong-metal.you_are_b:
Mu holds you the way a mountain holds ore. Solid, loyal, unflustered. You never have to guess where you stand with Mu. Except, apparently, on this.

Yeon: You'd have the "what are we" talk tonight, settle it, move on by breakfast.

Bom: Mu needs time to think. Push, and Mu goes still. You read that as dodging and get blunter.

Yeon: Mu doesn't show hurt easily, so Mu quietly digs in. Short texts both sides. Zero apologies. The whole thing freezes.

Bom: To a mountain, your urgency feels like being shoved before it's ready.

Make the question clear and let Mu set the pace: "I'd like us to be official. Think about it, and tell me when you're ready." Then actually wait. Patience isn't your talent, but it's the respect Mu responds to. Meanwhile, add one personal line to your messages. Mu notices. Then: your line.

mu-earth-and-sin-metal.title: Eleven hints. The mountain caught zero.
mu-earth-and-sin-metal.you_are_a:
Sin is the gem your mountain wants to protect. Sharp, elegant, a bit precious. And Sin finds your steadiness restful. Good match. Also: a lot of missed hints.

Yeon: Sin mentions a friend whose partner planned a surprise weekend. Posts a song that clearly means something. Goes cooler when you skip the haircut compliment.

Bom: You miss all of it. Not because you don't care. Mountains take things at face value.

Yeon: Sin feels unappreciated. You feel graded on an exam you never saw. Sin critiques your same jacket, your same Thursday. You start finding Sin high-maintenance.

Bom: Your devotion is real. Sin needs to see it said out loud.

Compliment specifically first. Not "you look nice". "That green really suits you." Then: "I'd like us to be together, officially. Is that you too?" And ask Sin directly if there's anything they've been hinting at. There will be a list. Next: your line.
mu-earth-and-sin-metal.you_are_b:
Mu is a mountain guarding a gem, and you're the gem. They carry your bags, fix your bike, show up on time.

Yeon: Lovely. Also deeply unromantic in how it's said. Which is mostly: not at all.

Bom: You've mentioned your friend's partner planning a surprise. Posted a song. Gone quieter when Mu forgot to comment on the outfit.

Yeon: Mu missed every single hint. Not from not caring. Mu takes everything at face value. A mountain doesn't do subtext.

Bom: You feel unappreciated. Mu feels like they're failing a test they were never handed. And when you critique Mu's simplicity, Mu finds you hard to please.

Plain words save months here: "I like you a lot. I want us to be exclusive and call it a relationship. And I'd love more compliments, specific ones. Could you do that?" And understand that Mu's short reply still means care. Then: your line.

mu-earth-and-im-water.title: The booked table vs the midnight flight
mu-earth-and-im-water.you_are_a:
Im is the river you can't stop watching. Big, clever, restless. Books flights at midnight. Quits things on a whim. You admire it. It also makes you slightly nervous.

Yeon: So you build a dam. A regular night. A booked table. A plan for next month.

Bom: Im feels contained and pushes back. Cancels, changes, suggests something else. You get frustrated by the shifting. Im gets bored by the routine.

Yeon: Money becomes a battlefield. You want to save for something. Im wants to spend it on an experience. Tonight.

Bom: Under all of it, "what is this" gets lost. Your consistency can feel like a cage to Im.

Allow some irregularity, and say clearly what you can't live without: "I don't need us to plan everything. I just need to know this is real between us. Where are you on that?" Then ask Im what freedom they need, and see if your mountain can make room for some. Next: your line.
mu-earth-and-im-water.you_are_b:
Mu is the dam to your river. Steady, solid, quietly immovable. You love how calm they are. You also want to shake things up every single time.

Yeon: Same restaurant. Same Thursday. A plan made three weeks ahead. Your soul leaves your body.

Bom: Mu books a table for next Friday and you feel boxed in, so you change it. Mu gets frustrated. You find routine boring. Mu finds your changes unreliable.

Yeon: Mu saves. You spend on experiences. And "what are we" sits under all of it, because asking feels like signing up for more structure.

Bom: A mountain can read your spontaneity as not taking this seriously.

Send something steady first. Keep a plan you made. Turn up on time. Then: "I know I'm all over the place. But I want to be with you. Can we work out how much structure we each need?" And let Mu keep a few plans without you rewriting them. Then: your line.

Respond to the feeling first. If Gye says "I've been anxious about us", say "I'm glad you told me" before anything else. Then: "I want to be with you. Properly. Is that what you'd like?" Don't fix. Just hold. Next: your line.

Yeon: You speak feelings. Mu speaks facts. You send a poetic message about the rain reminding you of them. Mu replies "yes, bring an umbrella tomorrow."

Bom: You feel unseen. Mu genuinely meant it as love.

Yeon: Share a worry about where this is going, and Mu offers a plan instead of comfort. Your shifting moods look like changeability to Mu.

Bom: A mountain only reads the literal layer.

Appreciate Mu's steadiness for what it is, then say it without the poem: "I'd like us to be together, properly. I need you to tell me how you feel, not just what to do. Can you do that for me?" Mu responds best to plain requests. Give one. Then: your line.
